description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:151-154

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct MemoryBackend {
    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner>>,
}
```

The `#[derive(Clone)]` produces a `Clone` impl that clones the
`Arc`, producing another handle to the same shared state. This is
intentional — the workspace pattern across all extension-server
siblings is `Arc<Mutex<Inner>>` for shared-state mock backends.

But the rustdoc on `MemoryBackend` (`memory.rs:147-150`) says:

> A fully in-memory implementation of [`SharingBackend`].
>
> Stores objects as serialized JSON; each mutation bumps a monotonic
> state counter and records a change log entry.

Nothing about Clone. A caller who reads this and writes:

```rust
let b1 = MemoryBackend::new_with_accounts(&[\"acc1\"]);
let b2 = b1.clone();
// expects b1 and b2 to be independent
b2.create_object::<Principal>(&(), &Id::from(\"acc1\"), \"c1\", p).await?;
// surprise: b1 now sees the same Principal
```

…sees their assumption violated silently. The mutex inside the
shared `Arc` means concurrent access from b1 and b2 is safe, but
the semantic question of \"do these share state\" is not in the
docs.

The canonical mail-server has the same shape and the same gap.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a downstream
test author writes a parameterized test that builds a `MemoryBackend`
once, clones it across test cases for \"independent state\", and gets
test-cross-contamination that is hard to diagnose because both
clones report identical `get_objects` results.

Resolution: add one sentence to the `MemoryBackend` rustdoc making
the sharing semantics explicit. The pattern is `Arc`-style cheap
clone for sharing across tasks; deep clones for independence
require building a second backend from scratch.

Note: propagating this doc to the canonical mail-server and the
other siblings would be a separate workspace-wide sweep bead — file
that follow-up if accepted here.
notes: Added Clone semantics paragraph to MemoryBackend rustdoc: cheap Arc clone, mutations visible across clones, build a new instance via Self::new()/Self::default() for independent state. Matches canonical jmap-mail-server pattern; aligned in shape but documented here.
title: MemoryBackend::Clone semantics undocumented — Arc-shared state, not independent
